info.title: Auto-serving dom-renderer in Spring Boot and Quarkus

parts.text: Next up, we want to ensure that the dom-renderer is automatically server in spring boot and quarkus. It should not be up the applikations using pathland to figure out how to server it.
Let me explore the codebase to understand how the DOM renderer is currently served in Spring Boot and Quarkus.
I'll investigate how the DOM renderer is currently served in the Spring Boot and Quarkus starters.

input.prompt:
Explore the Pathland repo at /Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland to understand how the DOM renderer (TypeScript bundle, built to dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js, content-hashed as dom-renderer-<sha256>.js with pointer file _pathland/dom-renderer.current) is currently served in the Spring Boot starter and Quarkus extension.

I need a very thorough understanding. Please find and report:

1. In `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`: every file/class that serves or references static assets, the DOM renderer bundle, HTML, CSS, `_pathland/` paths, resource handlers, controllers, auto-configuration. Show the relevant code snippets with file paths and line numbers.

2. In `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/` and `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-deployment/`: same thing — everything that serves/references the DOM renderer bundle, assets, `_pathland/`, resource routing, SSR endpoints, WebSocket, static file handling. Show code snippets with paths and line numbers.

3. In `lib/java/pathland-server-core/`: how SSR renders HTML and what URLs/paths it emits for the DOM renderer script, CSS, assets. Any config/seam for asset serving. Show code.

4. How the demos (`lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/`, `lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/`) themselves serve the DOM renderer bundle currently. Do they have their own static resource dirs / controllers / config? Show all relevant files and snippets (application.properties, controllers, src/main/resources structure).

5. How the DOM renderer bundle gets built and copied (look under lib/typescript/, scripts/, pom.xml files, package.json, any maven plugins / npm scripts). Show the build wiring and where the bundle ends up (dist path, copied locations).

6. Any existing tests related to serving assets / DOM renderer / HTML rendering in these modules.

Report findings organized by module with concrete file paths, line numbers and code excerpts. Do not modify anything.

<task_result>
# Pathland DOM renderer / asset serving — full trace

Below is the end-to-end picture: which classes serve what, where the bundle lives, how the SSR emits its URLs, and how the bundle is built/copied. All paths are absolute.

---

## 0. Mental model: the emitted URL surface

The reserved framework prefix is `/_pathland` (`PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE`). Per mounted app the base becomes `/{mount}/_pathland` (`PathlandRegistry.base()`).

| Asset | Root mount URL | Mounted app URL (e.g. `/app2`) | Produced by |
|---|---|---|---|
| DOM renderer JS | `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<sha256-12>.js` | `/app2/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` | `PathlandSession.renderHtml` + `PathlandAssets` manifest |
| Base design CSS | `/_pathland/base-<sha256-12>.css` | `/app2/_pathland/base-<hash>.css` | `HtmlRenderer.renderLinked` + `BaseCss` |
| Icon glyph | `/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` | `/app2/_pathland/icons/<name>.svg` | Java/Rust HTML renderer icon table |
| Service worker | `/_pathland/sw.js` | `/app2/_pathland/sw.js` | app static resource / filter |
| Media assets | `/_pathland/assets/**` | typically same absolute path | demo hosts |
| WebSocket | `/_pathland/ws` | `/app2/_pathland/ws` | starter/extension sockets |

The SSR document carries `data-pathland-base="/_pathland"` (or `"/app2/_pathland"`), plus optional `data-pathland-service-worker="true"` and `data-pathland-ssr-scoped="true"`.

---

# 1. `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/`

## 1.1 `PathlandIndexController` — the SSR and framework-asset controller

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/java/dev/pathland/spring/PathlandIndexController.java`

This is the only Spring class that serves HTML/assets. There is **no `WebMvcConfigurer` and no `addResourceHandlers`** anywhere in the module; it uses explicit `@GetMapping`s.

**Configuration seams** (lines 50–81):

```java
@Controller
public class PathlandIndexController {                       // line 45

    @Value("${pathland.asset-dir:}")
    private String assetDir;                                  // lines 50-53

    @Value("${pathland.seo.enabled:true}") private boolean seoEnabled;
    @Value("${pathland.seo.site-name:}") private String seoSiteName;
    @Value("${pathland.seo.image:}") private String seoImage;
    ...
```

- `pathland.asset-dir` is an optional **filesystem directory** served under `/_pathland/**` (used by the Spring demo to serve extracted media with Range support).
- `/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` are real routes (lines 88–104).

**SPA catch-all** (lines 123–141):

```java
@GetMapping(value = "/{*path}", headers = "!Upgrade")
@ResponseBody
public ResponseEntity<String> index(HttpServletRequest request) {
    MountMatch match = host.match(request.getRequestURI());
    if (match == null) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    String html = match.registry().renderHtml(
            match.route(), request.getParameter("wid"), pageMetadata(request));
    return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(MediaType.TEXT_HTML).body(html);
}
```

`headers = "!Upgrade"` ensures WebSocket handshakes are not swallowed.

**Framework asset handler — the key one** (lines 161–234):

```java
@GetMapping(value = {"/_pathland/**", "/{app}/_pathland/**"}, headers = "!Upgrade")
@ResponseBody
public ResponseEntity<?> framework(HttpServletRequest request) throws IOException {
    String uri = request.getRequestURI();
    int idx = uri.indexOf("/_pathland/");
    if (idx < 0) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    String file = uri.substring(idx + "/_pathland/".length());

    if ("sw.js".equals(file)) {
        Resource sw = classpathFrameworkResource(file);
        if (sw == null || !sw.exists()) return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
        try (InputStream in = sw.getInputStream()) {
            return ResponseEntity.ok()
                .contentType(new MediaType("application", "javascript"))
                .header("Service-Worker-Allowed", "/")
                .cacheControl(CacheControl.noCache())
                .body(in.readAllBytes());
        }
    }

    Resource resource = classpathFrameworkResource(file);
    if (resource == null) resource = diskAsset(file);
    if (resource == null || !resource.exists()) {
        ResponseEntity<?> cssResponse = baseCss(file);
        if (cssResponse != null) return cssResponse;
        ResponseEntity<?> icon = iconGlyph(file);
        if (icon != null) return icon;
        return ResponseEntity.notFound().build();
    }
    MediaType type = MediaTypeFactory.getMediaType(file)
            .orElse(MediaType.APPLICATION_OCTET_STREAM);
    String rangeHeader = request.getHeader(HttpHeaders.RANGE);
    if (rangeHeader != null && !rangeHeader.isEmpty()) {
        return rangeResponse(resource, type, rangeHeader);
    }
    try (InputStream in = resource.getInputStream()) {
        return ResponseEntity.ok().contentType(type)
            .header(HttpHeaders.ACCEPT_RANGES, "bytes")
            .cacheControl(CacheControl.maxAge(Duration.ofDays(7)).cachePublic().immutable())
            .body(in.readAllBytes());
    }
}
```

Resolution order: **classpath → disk → renderer-owned CSS → renderer-owned icons**:

- `classpathFrameworkResource` (lines 281–285):

```java
ClassPathResource resource = new ClassPathResource("static/_pathland/" + file);
return resource.exists() ? resource : null;
```

- `diskAsset` (lines 287–299): reads `${pathland.asset-dir}`, normalizes and guards against traversal.
- `baseCss` (lines 236–255): returns `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` when `file.equals(HtmlRenderer.baseCssName())`, with `max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- `iconGlyph` (lines 257–279): `icons/<name>.svg` via `HtmlRenderer.iconSvg`, `max-age=30 days, immutable`.
- `rangeResponse` (lines 301–347): full byte-range support, `206 Partial Content`, `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges.

## 1.2 Auto-configuration

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/java/dev/pathland/spring/PathlandAutoConfiguration.java`

- `@AutoConfiguration` + `@EnableWebSocket` (lines 54–56).
- `PathlandHost` bean reads `pathland.debug-html` and `pathland.service-worker` (lines 110–126):

```java
@Bean(destroyMethod = "shutdown")
@ConditionalOnMissingBean
public PathlandHost pathlandHost(..., 
        @Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}") boolean debugHtml,
        @Value("${pathland.service-worker:false}") boolean serviceWorker) { ... }
```

- WebSocket registration at each app base (lines 128–151):

```java
return registry -> host.registries().forEach(r -> {
    var registration = registry.addHandler(new PathlandSocket(r), r.base() + "/ws");
    ...
});
```

- `PathlandIndexController` is registered as a bean (lines 153–158) so apps can override it.

## 1.3 Registration / metadata files

- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/META-INF/spring/org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.AutoConfiguration.imports` line 1:
  `dev.pathland.spring.PathlandAutoConfiguration`
- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/META-INF/spring.factories` lines 1–2: registers `PathlandEnvironmentPostProcessor` (forwarded-header default; not asset-related).

## 1.4 WebSocket path

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/java/dev/pathland/spring/PathlandSocket.java` lines 35–38:

```java
public PathlandSocket(PathlandRegistry registry) {
    this.registry = registry;
    this.path = registry.base() + "/ws";
}
```

So root → `/_pathland/ws`, mounted → `/app2/_pathland/ws`.

## 1.5 What the starter jar itself contains

**It does not contain the DOM renderer bundle.** Its `src/main/resources` has only `META-INF/spring.factories` and the auto-config import. The demo/consumer must put the bundle + `dom-renderer.current` under its own `src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`. Spring Boot’s default static handler also maps `classpath:/static/**`, but the explicit `/_pathland/**` controller mapping takes precedence.

Test-only fixture: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/test/resources/static/_pathland/sw.js` (no JS bundle).

---

# 2. `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/` + `pathland-quarkus-deployment/`

## 2.1 How Quarkus serves static files

Quarkus serves `META-INF/resources/**` from the application (and dependency jars) **before JAX-RS**, so the global `/_pathland/**` bundle is normally served by Quarkus’s static-resource handler, not by `IndexResource`. The extension only adds explicit JAX-RS routes for things that have no static file (CSS/icons) and for **mounted** app bases (`/{app}/_pathland/**`), because Quarkus’s static handler only serves the global `/_pathland/**` tree.

## 2.2 `IndexResource` — SSR + mounted-base framework files + CSS/icons

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/IndexResource.java`

`@Path("/")` at line 39.

**Root page** (lines 74–80):

```java
@GET
@Produces(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
public Response index(@QueryParam("wid") String wid, @Context UriInfo uri,
        @Context HttpHeaders headers) {
    return render("/", wid, uri, headers);
}
```

`/robots.txt` and `/sitemap.xml` at lines 82–102.

**Deep-link catch-all with framework-path interception** (lines 104–123):

```java
@GET
@Path("{path:(?!_pathland)(?!q/).*}")
@Produces(MediaType.TEXT_HTML)
public Response deep(@PathParam("path") String path, @QueryParam("wid") String wid,
        @Context UriInfo uri, @Context HttpHeaders headers) throws IOException {
    int framework = path.indexOf("/_pathland/");
    if (framework >= 0) {
        return frameworkFile(path.substring(framework + "/_pathland/".length()));
    }
    return render("/" + path, wid, uri, headers);
}
```

The negative lookahead excludes:
- the **global** `/_pathland/**` (left to Quarkus static resources),
- Quarkus non-application `/q/**`.

But a **mounted** path like `/ad/_pathland/dom-renderer-….js` is caught here and routed to `frameworkFile`.

**Renderer-owned icon and CSS routes** (lines 193–210):

```java
@GET
@Path("/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg")
@Produces("image/svg+xml")
public Response icon(@PathParam("name") String name) { return iconResponse(name); }

@GET
@Path("/_pathland/{name}.css")
@Produces("text/css")
public Response baseCss(@PathParam("name") String name) {
    Response css = baseCssResponse(name + ".css");
    return css != null ? css : Response.status(Response.Status.NOT_FOUND).build();
}
```

**Mounted-app framework file resolution** (lines 212–235):

```java
private Response frameworkFile(String file) throws IOException {
    // Quarkus web static lives in META-INF/resources (classpath resource root), so the
    // shared `/_pathland/**` mount resolves as /META-INF/resources/_pathland/<file>.
    try (InputStream in = getClass().getResourceAsStream(
            "/META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + file)) {
        if (in != null) {
            return Response.ok(in.readAllBytes()).type(mediaTypeOf(file)).build();
        }
    }
    Response css = baseCssResponse(file);
    if (css != null) return css;
    if (file.startsWith("icons/") && file.endsWith(".svg")
            && file.substring("icons/".length(), file.length() - ".svg".length()).indexOf('/') < 0) {
        return iconResponse(file.substring("icons/".length(), file.length() - ".svg".length()));
    }
    return Response.status(Response.Status.NOT_FOUND).build();
}
```

- `baseCssResponse` (lines 237–255) serves the content-hashed CSS with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`.
- `iconResponse` (lines 257–268) serves SVG with `max-age=2592000, immutable`.
- `mediaTypeOf` (lines 270–284) maps `.js`, `.svg`, `.mp3`, `.mp4`, else octet-stream.

Note: `frameworkFile` has **no Range handling** and **no filesystem asset-dir seam**; it reads classpath bytes.

## 2.3 `ServiceWorkerFilter`

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/ServiceWorkerFilter.java`

Quarkus’s static handler doesn’t send `Service-Worker-Allowed` / `no-cache`, so this filter intercepts `/_pathland/sw.js` (and mounted bases) before routes.

Lines 42–69:

```java
private static final String RESOURCE = "META-INF/resources/_pathland/sw.js";
private static final String PATH_SUFFIX = "/_pathland/sw.js";

void init(@Observes Filters filters) {
    filters.register(context -> {
        if (!context.normalizedPath().endsWith(PATH_SUFFIX)) { context.next(); return; }
        byte[] script = readResource();
        if (script == null) { context.next(); return; } // fail open
        context.response()
            .putHeader("Content-Type", "text/javascript;charset=UTF-8")
            .putHeader("Service-Worker-Allowed", "/")
            .putHeader("Cache-Control", "no-cache")
            .end(Buffer.buffer(script));
    }, 100);
}
```

Classloading fallback (lines 72–102): thread-context loader → this class’s loader → system loader. This is needed because the extension runtime loader may not see the application’s `META-INF/resources` copy.

## 2.4 WebSocket endpoints

- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/PathlandSocket.java` line 39: `@WebSocket(path = "/_pathland/ws")` (root app).
- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/MountedPathlandSocket.java` line 36: `@WebSocket(path = "/{app}/_pathland/ws")` (mounted apps). The `{app}` path param resolves the registry at lines 112–115.

## 2.5 CDI host wiring / config

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/PathlandRegistryProducer.java`

- `pathland.debug-html` default `false` (lines 73–75).
- `pathland.service-worker` default `false` (lines 77–79).
- Host construction passes the flag (lines 96–107):

```java
@Produces @Singleton
PathlandHost host(PathlandTelemetry telemetry) {
    ...
    return new PathlandHost(list, StateStores.redisOrFallback(new InMemoryStateStore()),
            debugHtml, telemetry, serviceWorker);
}
```

## 2.6 Extension resources

- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/sw.js` — the **only** asset the extension jar ships; it is the service-worker fallback. **No DOM renderer bundle is bundled in the extension.**
- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/beans.xml`
- `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/quarkus-extension.yaml`

## 2.7 Deployment module

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus-deployment/src/main/java/dev/pathland/quarkus/deployment/PathlandProcessor.java`

- Default CSP (lines 26–38) has `script-src 'self'`, `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`, `img-src 'self' data:`, `media-src 'self'`, `worker-src 'self'`.
- `securityDefaults()` (lines 59–81) contributes Quarkus runtime defaults for CORS, forwarded headers, WebSocket size caps, CSP and `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options`.
- `PathlandKotlinProcessor.java` is just a feature-build marker.

There is **no custom `Route`/`StaticHandler` in the extension**; the demo adds one for media assets (see §4).

---

# 3. `lib/java/pathland-server-core/` — SSR and emitted URLs

## 3.1 Framework base resolution

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandSession.java` lines 57–60:

```java
/** The reserved framework path prefix (spec): host system endpoints ... live under
 *  {@code /_pathland/**} ... */
public static final String PATHLAND_BASE = "/_pathland";
```

`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandRegistry.java` lines 142–145:

```java
public String base() {
    return "/".equals(mountPath)
            ? PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE
            : mountPath + PathlandSession.PATHLAND_BASE;
}
```

So `/` → `/_pathland`, `/app2` → `/app2/_pathland`.

`PathlandHost.match` (lines 100–111) chooses the longest mount and returns the mount-stripped route; `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml` (lines 197–222) creates a throwaway `PathlandSession` with that `base()` and renders.

## 3.2 The actual SSR HTML construction

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandSession.java` lines 444–475:

```java
public String renderHtml(boolean serviceWorker, boolean ssrScoped, PageMetadata pageMetadata) {
    HtmlRenderer renderer = HtmlRenderer.tryInstance();
    if (renderer == null) {
        return "<!DOCTYPE html>... Pathland renderer unavailable ...";
    }
    ProtocolFrame frame = ssrFrame();
    DocumentMeta meta = documentMeta(pageMetadata);
    String html = debugHtml
            ? renderer.renderLinkedDebug(frame, rootId, base, meta)
            : renderer.renderLinked(frame, rootId, base, meta);

    String htmlAttrs = " data-pathland-base=\"" + base + "\""
            + (serviceWorker ? " data-pathland-service-worker=\"true\"" : "")
            + (ssrScoped ? " data-pathland-ssr-scoped=\"true\"" : "");
    String integrity = PathlandAssets.bundleIntegrity();
    String integrityAttr = integrity.isEmpty() ? "" : " integrity=\"" + integrity + "\"";
    return injectHtmlAttributes(html, htmlAttrs)
            .replace("</body>", "<script src=\"" + base + "/" + PathlandAssets.bundleName()
                    + "\"" + integrityAttr + " defer></script></body>");
}
```

Key facts:
- **The script tag is injected by `PathlandSession`** just before `</body>`.
- **`data-pathland-base` is injected on the `<html>` tag** by `injectHtmlAttributes` (lines 503–518).
- The CSS link is emitted by the renderer, not by `PathlandSession` (see below).
- If `HtmlRenderer` is unavailable, an “unavailable” document is returned with no script.

## 3.3 CSS `<link>` emission

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/HtmlRenderer.java`

- `baseCssName()` / `baseCss()` lines 73–81.
- `renderLinked(...)` lines 97–110.
- `linkedCssHead` lines 437–444:

```java
private static String linkedCssHead(String cssBase) {
    String base = cssBase;
    while (base.endsWith("/")) base = base.substring(0, base.length() - 1);
    return "<link rel=\"stylesheet\" href=\"" + Format.escapeHtmlAttr(base) + "/"
            + BaseCss.builtinCssName() + "\">";
}
```

`renderLinked` falls back to inline CSS if either the base or the CSS name is empty (lines 106–108).

`BaseCss` (`/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-render-html/src/main/java/dev/pathland/render/html/BaseCss.java` lines 12–25) reads the classpath resources `/dev/pathland/render/html/base.css` and `base.css.name`.

Icons: `HtmlRenderer.iconSvg(name)` lines 158–168 renders `/<svg>` from the `Icons` table.

## 3.4 `PathlandAssets` — content-hashed bundle manifest

**File:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/PathlandAssets.java`

Manifest lookup paths (lines 38–45):

```java
static final String MANIFEST = "dom-renderer.current";
static final String FALLBACK = "dom-renderer.js";

private static final String[] MANIFEST_PATHS = {
    "META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + MANIFEST,  // Quarkus demo
    "static/_pathland/" + MANIFEST,               // Spring Boot demo
    "_pathland/" + MANIFEST,                      // generic
};
```

Resolution semantics (lines 110–127):

```java
static Manifest resolveManifest(Lookup lookup) {
    for (String path : MANIFEST_PATHS) {
        try (InputStream in = lookup.open(path)) {
            ...
            List<String> lines = readLines(in, 2);
            String name = lines.isEmpty() ? "" : lines.get(0).trim();
            if (validBundleName(name)) {
                String integrity = lines.size() > 1 ? lines.get(1).trim() : "";
                return new Manifest(name, validIntegrity(integrity) ? integrity : "");
            }
        } catch (IOException ignored) {}
    }
    return new Manifest(FALLBACK, "");
}
```

- The first line is the content-hashed filename.
- The second line is an optional `sha384-<base64>` SRI digest.
- Fallback is the pre-hash literal `dom-renderer.js` with no integrity.
- Resolution is classloader-aware (thread context first, then own loader, then system — lines 71–102, 129–142), cached per loader.
- `bundleName()` / `bundleIntegrity()` at lines 61–69 are the only public-ish seams used by `PathlandSession`.

## 3.5 What server-core does *not* serve

`pathland-server-core` contains **no HTTP server / asset handler**. It only emits URLs and resolves the bundle name. Serving is the host framework’s job:
- Spring: `PathlandIndexController.framework(...)`.
- Quarkus: static `META-INF/resources` + `IndexResource.frameworkFile(...)`.
- Media assets referenced by views are absolute (`/_pathland/assets/...`) and are served by the demo hosts; server-core does not rewrite them.

Proxy sessions also construct origin URLs using the reserved base: `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/java/dev/pathland/server/proxy/ProxySession.java` line 503 appends `/_pathland/ws?wid=...`.

---

# 4. Demo modules — how the bundle is actually served today

## 4.1 Spring Boot demo

**Module:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-demo/`

Files present:

```text
src/main/java/dev/pathland/demo/spring/SpringDemoApplication.java
src/main/resources/application.properties
src/main/resources/static/_pathland/dom-renderer-77eb5c6fc78d.js
src/main/resources/static/_pathland/dom-renderer.current
src/main/resources/static/_pathland/sw.js
```

There is **no `src/test`** and **no demo-local controller/config class**.

`SpringDemoApplication` (lines 27–33) sets the asset-dir system property before boot:

```java
public static void main(String[] args) {
    // The demo's media + icons are served from a temp-dir extraction of the
    // shared demo-views jar ... extract once, before the app boots.
    System.setProperty("pathland.asset-dir", DemoAssets.extractToTemp().toString());
    SpringApplication.run(SpringDemoApplication.class, args);
}
```

It then declares only `PathlandApp` / `MountedApp` beans (lines 35–45). The DOM bundle is served by the starter’s `PathlandIndexController.framework(...)` from `classpath:/static/_pathland/…`; no demo resource handler exists.

`application.properties` relevant lines:

- lines 5–9: `pathland.debug-html=true`, `spring.web.resources.cache.period=7d` (comment says “served from a disk extraction via DemoAssetsConfig” — **that class does not exist**; the actual mechanism is the `pathland.asset-dir` system property in `main`).
- lines 26–31: SEO defaults.

Committed manifest (`static/_pathland/dom-renderer.current`):

```text
dom-renderer-77eb5c6fc78d.js
REDACTED
```

## 4.2 Quarkus demo

**Module:** `/Users/michael/Development/michaelkrog/Pathland/lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/`

   - Quarkus: global `/_pathland/**` is served by Quarkus’s static `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS; mounted `/{app}/_pathland/**` is intercepted by `IndexResource.deep` → `frameworkFile`.

6: // so a new bundle always changes the URL — the scripts are served with

8: // cache. A tiny pointer manifest `dom-renderer.current` is written next to the
9: // copies so the SSR layer emits the right <script src> without re-hashing:

12: //   sha384-<base64>
13: //
14: // The second line is the Subresource Integrity digest for the script tag. Stale
15: // `dom-renderer-*.js` (and the pre-hash fixed `dom-renderer.js`) are pruned so

28: const manifest = "dom-renderer.current";

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Spring Boot Starter</name>
    <description>
        Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live 16-byte opcode
        deltas over /ws, per-session state. Add this dependency and a PathlandApp bean and
        you have a running app.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-server-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-web</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-websocket</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-actuator</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <!-- The OTel API is referenced only to build the optional tracing decorator; an
             OpenTelemetry bean exists only when the app adds micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-api</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.springframework.boot</groupId>
            <artifactId>spring-boot-starter-test</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <!-- Tests prove a Java host can mount a Kotlin-authored view. Production stays
             DSL-neutral; applications add their chosen authoring DSL themselves. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"

    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus</name>
    <description>
        Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live 16-byte opcode deltas over
        /ws, per-session state, plus the Kotlin authoring DSL. Add this extension and a
        PathlandApp bean and you have a running app. Author the root view with the Kotlin
        DSL in pathland-view-core; Java hosts mount Kotlin views.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-server-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-kotlin</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-rest</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-websockets-next</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-smallrye-health</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <!-- The OTel API is referenced only to build the optional tracing decorator; a
             Tracer bean exists only when the app adds quarkus-opentelemetry. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.opentelemetry</groupId>
            <artifactId>opentelemetry-api</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit5</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <!-- A registry backend so /q/metrics exists in the starter's tests. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-extension-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>extension-descriptor</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <capabilities>
                        <provides>dev.pathland.quarkus</provides>
                        <provides>dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin</provides>
                    </capabilities>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

         `mvn test`, `mvn package`, or the Maven Central release. Rust is only needed

         GTK/Qt renderer dylibs) and for regenerating shared artifacts (the protocol
         manifest, engine traces, HTML golden fixtures, and TS constants).

         rebuild itself — the design CSS/tokens (npm build) and the DOM bundle
         (npm build:all) — plus the render-html module's embedded CSS resources (its
         Maven copy step does not run under IntelliJ's own build). IntelliJ then

         imported, so no ~/.m2 is used) and copies the refreshed bundle + its
         dom-renderer.current manifest into target/classes on Build Project. Invoke with

        pathland-render-html, live 16-byte opcode deltas over raw WebSocket, and

        the starter dependency + a PathlandApp bean returning the Kotlin MusicPlayerView.

        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-spring-boot-starter</artifactId>

             opt-in via micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel (see the application.properties flag). -->
        <dependency>

            <artifactId>micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.micrometer</groupId>
            <artifactId>micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel</artifactId>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>

                <artifactId>spring-boot-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>repackage</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-quarkus-demo</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <!-- Demo application — not published to Maven Central. -->
    <properties>
        <maven.deploy.skip>true</maven.deploy.skip>
        <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
    </properties>

    <name>Pathland Quarkus Demo</name>
    <description>
        Quarkus demonstration app consuming the Pathland libraries: SSR
        (pathland-render-html) for instant first paint, then live 16-byte opcode deltas +
        events over WebSocket, with cross-platform state persisted through StateStore
        (Redis with an in-memory fallback). The host is Java and mounts the shared Kotlin
        MusicPlayerView; a second mount demonstrates a Kotlin-only authored view.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-quarkus</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-demo-views-kotlin</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <!-- Observability (issue #62): a Prometheus scrape endpoint at /q/metrics; health
             at /q/health comes from the starter. OpenTelemetry spans are OPT-IN — add
             io.quarkus:quarkus-opentelemetry to enable them (see the application.properties
             note); the starter wires the tracing decorator when the extension is present. -->
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-micrometer-registry-prometheus</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-logging-json</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
            <artifactId>quarkus-junit5</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
                <artifactId>maven-surefire-plugin</artifactId>
                <configuration>
                    <argLine>-Dpathland.proxy.snapshot-timeout-ms=10000</argLine>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>io.quarkus</groupId>
                <artifactId>quarkus-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>build</goal>
                        </goals>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>
</project>

parts.text:
Now I have a clear picture. The core change: bundle the DOM renderer JS + manifest + sw.js into the published libraries (Spring starter and Quarkus extension), so consumers don't have to add it.

Key design decisions:

1. Where to store the committed bundle in the repo. Options:
   - Add copies in the Spring starter's `src/main/resources/static/_pathland/` and Quarkus extension's `src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`.
   - Or a shared module (e.g., a new `pathland-dom-renderer` jar resource-only module) that both depend on. This would avoid duplicating the bundle bytes in two jars and keep a single content-hashed copy. But it adds a module. Also the Quarkus extension's static resources are served from dependency jars, so a shared jar works. Spring too via classpath `static/`... actually Spring Boot's static resource handling merges classpath:/static/ across all jars? Yes, ResourceHttpRequestHandler resolves classpath:/static/ locations across the classpath — but the starter's controller explicitly uses `new ClassPathResource("static/_pathland/" + file)` which resolves from the app classloader and will find it in any jar on the classpath. So a shared resource-only jar works for both.

Actually, `PathlandAssets` manifest lookup already has paths: `META-INF/resources/_pathland/`, `static/_pathland/`, `_pathland/`. If we put the bundle in the starter jar as `static/_pathland/`, and the extension jar as `META-INF/resources/_pathland/`, then `PathlandAssets` resolves them. If we use a shared jar with both locations? Hmm.

Let me think about the simplest robust approach consistent with the existing pattern:

- The repo already commits generated artifacts (CSS under Rust assets, bundle in demo resources). The natural approach: extend `copy-to-demos.mjs` to also copy the bundle + manifest into:
  - `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland/`
  - `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`
  and stop copying into the demos (or keep demos as-is? better to remove duplication and have demos rely on the libraries). This directly makes the library ship the bundle.

- Then remove the committed bundle from the demos (Spring `static/_pathland/`, Quarkus `META-INF/resources/_pathland/`) so there's one source. Keep `sw.js`? The Quarkus extension already ships sw.js; the Spring starter should also ship sw.js so service worker works out of the box. Currently Spring demo ships sw.js. So move it to the starter.

But wait: there is a subtlety with Quarkus static resources. Quarkus serves static resources from `META-INF/resources` of dependency jars? Let me verify. Quarkus documentation says static resources are served from `META-INF/resources` directory in the application classpath, including dependencies. Indeed extensions like Swagger UI put `META-INF/resources` in their runtime jar. So the extension's `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` bundle will be served under `/_pathland/`, good. And mounted app base uses `IndexResource.deep` → `frameworkFile` which uses `getClass().getResourceAsStream("/META-INF/resources/_pathland/" + file)`. `getClass()` is IndexResource's class (in the extension jar), so getResourceAsStream resolves against the class's classloader which should see its own jar at least, and the TCCL? Actually `Class.getResourceAsStream` uses the class's classloader, which for an extension runtime class is the runtime classloader that can see all app + extension resources typically. But the current `ServiceWorkerFilter` has a fallback chain because "the extension runtime loader may not see the consuming app's META-INF/resources copy". Now, the resource we control is in the extension's own jar, so `IndexResource.class.getResourceAsStream` will definitely see it. Good. But the ordering: app-provided override should win. So `frameworkFile` should first look at the app's classpath resources (via TCCL) then fall back to the extension's own resource. Actually `Class.getResourceAsStream` on the extension class might already see app resources if same loader. To be safe, mimic ServiceWorkerFilter's chain and prefer app copies.

Hmm, but there's a catch: for the global `/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js` in Quarkus, if both the app and extension provide the resource, Quarkus static resource serving might pick one deterministically. If the app provides a stale/older bundle, it could shadow the extension's. That's acceptable (app override). But the SSR manifest must match the served bundle. `PathlandAssets` resolves through TCCL first, so app's manifest wins. Consistent.

For Spring, `classpathFrameworkResource` uses `new ClassPathResource("static/_pathland/" + file)` which uses TCCL of the current thread by default (ClassPathResource with no classloader uses the default ClassUtils.getDefaultClassLoader() = TCCL). So app override wins. Good.

2. Should we keep the demos' copies? If the starter/extension now ship the bundle, the demos can drop theirs. But the CI drift guard currently diffs the demo resources. We'll update the guard to diff the library resources instead. Keeping demos' copies would cause duplicate resource collision (app copy shadows library copy) but is harmless; however it defeats the purpose of "not up to the applications". Better to remove from demos to prove it works.

3. Build/refresh wiring: `copy-to-demos.mjs` should be renamed conceptually (but the script name can stay to avoid churn, or rename to `copy-to-libs.mjs`? The npm script `copy-to-demos` is referenced in CI and parent pom). Renaming touches package.json, CI, parent pom comment. Could keep name but change targets. I'd lean rename to `copy-to-jars` or `copy-to-runtime`? Let's think. Minimal churn: keep script name `copy-to-demos.mjs` but change targets and update comments — misleading. Better rename to `copy-to-libs.mjs` and update package.json scripts (`copy-to-demos` → maybe keep alias). Since it's a plan, propose renaming to `copy-to-libraries.mjs`, with npm script `copy-to-libs`, and update CI + refresh comment. But careful: CI workflow uses `npm run copy-to-demos`. parts.text:
Now I have enough to form the plan. Let me consider the exact approach and whether to create a shared resource jar vs duplicated copies.

Option A: Duplicate bundle into both library jars.
- Pros: no new module, simplest conceptually, each library self-contained.
- Cons: bundle bytes duplicated in repo (~150KB x2) and two jars; drift risk between the two copies; copy script handles both. But it already duplicates into two demos, so precedent.

Option B: New resource-only module `pathland-dom-renderer` (jar) containing:
- `static/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js`, `static/_pathland/dom-renderer.current` (for Spring), and `META-INF/resources/_pathland/...` (for Quarkus static). Both starter and quarkus depend on it. Actually can a single jar hold both layouts, duplicating the bytes within the same jar? Still duplication within jar. Or rely on classpath location independence: Spring controller uses `classpath:static/_pathland/`; Quarkus static uses `META-INF/resources`. Could make Spring's controller also look at `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` as a fallback, and Quarkus's global static handler requires `META-INF/resources`. Then one jar could contain the bundle only under `META-INF/resources/_pathland/`, and:
  - Quarkus: static handler serves it.
  - Spring: modify `classpathFrameworkResource` to try `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` too (and `PathlandAssets` already probes it first).
  - Mounted Quarkus path: `frameworkFile` uses `/META-INF/resources/_pathland/`.
  This yields a single copy in a shared module, no duplication. And it's clean: a resource-only "web client" jar shipped to both.

But adding a new module to publish to Maven Central has overhead (pom, release config). Is that desired? It decouples the bundle from the starters and gives a clear artifact `pathland-dom-renderer`. The user's ask: "ensure the dom-renderer is automatically served in spring boot and quarkus. It should not be up to the applications using pathland to figure out how to serve it." A shared resource jar is elegant.

However, introducing a new published module is a bigger change and touches release. Option A (copy into starter + quarkus jars) is more direct and self-contained, and both jars are already published. But duplicated file in git. The existing `copy-to-demos` already copies to two places and CI enforces no drift by regenerating. Duplicating in two library modules is consistent, and each jar works standalone (starter doesn't depend on quarkus).

Which does the user likely prefer? Hard to know. I should ask a clarifying question about artifact strategy (new shared jar vs duplicate in each). Also ask whether to remove demo copies. Also ask about custom override support: should app-provided copies still take precedence? Likely yes.

Also, consider Quarkus static resource serving: need to verify that Quarkus serves `META-INF/resources` from extension/runtime dependency jars. Let me confirm quickly via search of quarkus behavior or existing assets in dependencies. The servlet/vertx-http static resources handler uses `META-INF/resources` merged from all classpath entries. I'm fairly confident. But for mounted bases it doesn't serve global. Fine.

But there's a concern: Quarkus `quarkus.http.static-resources` default `max-age` maybe. Not crucial.

Another concern for Quarkus: The `IndexResource.deep` negative lookahead excludes paths starting with `_pathland`, leaving global to static resources. If Quarkus static serving of dependency jar resources doesn't work (e.g., in native image), we'd need explicit routes. Native image resource inclusion may need registration. `quarkus:build` native might not include jar resources automatically; but static resources from `META-INF/resources` are typically included. Could add an explicit fallback in `IndexResource` for the global `/_pathland/**` by changing the negative lookahead? Actually safer: add explicit JAX-RS route for `/ _pathland/{file}`? But there's already `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` and `/_pathland/{name}.css`. We could add `/_pathland/{file}` for the JS. However Quarkus static resources are served before JAX-RS, so a JAX-RS route would only be a fallback. Could add `@Path("/_pathland/{file}")` for the bundle. But conflicts? Static handler runs first, so fine. Yet path matching precedence between the two existing JAX-RS routes: `/ _pathland/icons/{name}.svg` and `/_pathland/{name}.css` are more specific. Adding `/_pathland/{file}` likely fine.

Actually simpler robust approach: since `IndexResource` already serves mounted apps' framework files from classpath, and it has `frameworkFile`, we can also let global requests fall through to it if static doesn't serve. But the negative lookahead intentionally excludes `_pathland` so unknown global framework paths return a static 404 from Quarkus, not SSR. Hmm. We could narrow the lookahead or add an explicit global `@Path("/_pathland/{file}")`. I'd propose adding an explicit route as a belt-and-suspenders for native/test, while relying on static serving in JVM mode. But adding a route that returns the JS is harmless and guarantees behavior (static handler takes precedence if it serves). Wait — if static handler serves the file, the JAX-RS route never runs. If it doesn't, JAX-RS serves. Good.

But careful with JAX-RS path patterns: `@Path("/_pathland/{file}")` would also match `/ _pathland/icons/foo.svg`? No, icons is two segments. It would match single-segment JS and sw.js. Fine. But the existing `/_pathland/{name}.css` is a single segment too; precedence by literal suffix? Both are template expressions; JAX-RS sorts by literal chars. `{name}.css` has a literal suffix, likely more specific. Could instead use `@Path("/_pathland/{file:dom-renderer-.*\\.js}")` to be explicit, or just `/_pathland/{file}` and handle names in code. Keep it simple.

Wait, but the global `/_pathland/sw.js` is handled by ServiceWorkerFilter at priority 100 before routes, and static. Good.

For Spring: the `framework` controller already handles all `/_pathland/**` including bundle, so once the starter jar contains `static/_pathland/<file>`, it works. Good. Optionally add `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` fallback if shared jar chosen.

Now, another key issue: `PathlandAssets` manifest cache. It resolves once per classloader. If the bundle/manifest now lives in the starter jar, `PathlandAssets` (in server-core) finds `static/_pathland/dom-renderer.current` or `META-INF/resources/_pathland/...`. It already probes `META-INF/resources` first, then `static`. If both the demo app and library provide it (during transition), app wins (TCCL). But `openClasspath` uses a single classloader's `getResourceAsStream`, which returns the first match on the classpath—not necessarily deterministic ordering. Since app classes and dependency jars are on the same classloader in Spring Boot, resource order is classpath order (app classes first typically). Fine.

Also: if the Quarkus extension ships `META-INF/resources/_pathland/dom-renderer.current`, then `PathlandAssets` via TCCL sees it. In Quarkus, resources in dependency jars are visible to TCCL. Yes.

Now, the demo cleanup: Remove demo copies so the libraries prove they serve it. But then in Spring, the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` classpath includes the starter jar; `ClassPathResource("static/_pathland/...")` resolves. In Quarkus, the extension jar `META-INF/resources` is served. Good.

However, there's a catch for `pathland-spring-boot-starter` tests: tests have their own `src/test/resources/static/_pathland/sw.js`. If the starter jar (main resources) now also has `static/_pathland/sw.js`, during tests the test resources take precedence? Both same classpath; the test-classes dir typically comes before main classes, so test copy wins. Could remove the test fixture, but keep for override testing maybe.

Now, what about the CSS? Already shipped and served from renderer. Icons too. Only the JS bundle + sw.js + manifest are missing from libraries.

Let's also consider the Quarkus `ServiceWorkerFilter` already prefers app copy then extension copy; with extension shipping sw.js it works. For Spring, the starter's controller serves sw.js from `classpath:/static/_pathland/sw.js`; with the starter shipping it, works.

Now let's think about the copy script: rename to `copy-to-jars.mjs` or `copy-to-libs.mjs`. Targets:
- `lib/java/pathland-spring-boot-starter/src/main/resources/static/_pathland`
- `lib/java/pathland-quarkus/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/_pathland`
And optionally remove demo target copies (delete files). Update CI drift check to diff those library dirs. Update npm script name maybe keep `copy-to-demos` for compatibility? I'd rename to `copy-to-libs`, update package.json, CI, README, status docs, parent pom comment. But maybe keep the old npm script as alias to reduce breakage in docs? Let's propose rename and update references. Actually, the script name `copy-to-demos` appears in 9 places. Renaming is manageable. But user may not care. I'll include in plan, maybe keep `copy-to-demos` naming to minimize churn but update its purpose/comment. Hmm. Since the whole point is it's no longer demos, I'd rename. I'll flag it as a minor decision in the plan, defaulting to rename.

Alternative to copying in git: have Maven fetch the artifact. But repo already commits generated CSS and bundle; consistency says commit generated bundle into library resources.

Now, do we need to keep the demos' copies for color? No. Remove them. But be careful: the Quarkus demo currently relies on static resources from app `META-INF/resources` for the global bundle. With extension jar providing it, it should still work. Tests in `pathland-quarkus-demo` (SecurityHeadersTest) check `integrity="sha384-"` in HTML from manifest; the manifest now comes from the extension jar, still fine.

But there could be a subtle issue: `quarkus.http.static-resources.max-age=168h` in the demo only; library consumers won't have that. Our `IndexResource` static fallback can set proper cache headers for the bundle (immutable). But if Quarkus static handler serves it first, the max-age default maybe 24h or disabled. The content-hashed name means we want immutable. Quarkus static handler sets cache-control? Quarkus static resources sets `Cache-Control: public, max-age=...` based on config; default `max-age=86400` maybe. Not necessarily immutable. But this is a performance nuance, not correctness. Could add an explicit route/filter to force immutable caching for `dom-renderer-*.js` similar to `ServiceWorkerFilter`. Hmm. Spring controller sets 7d immutable. For consistency, maybe add a small filter or route to set immutable cache for hashed bundle and CSS/icons globally. But Quarkus static handler runs before JAX-RS, so can't set headers there via route. Could add a `ResponseFilter`? Or a `RouteFilter` (Vert.x) registered at higher precedence than static handler? `ServiceWorkerFilter` intercepts in `init(@Observes Filters filters)` at priority 100. But static handler ordering? They intercept specific path suffix. We could extend that filter to also handle the hashed bundle and set immutable. However, reading the resource bytes in a filter duplicates static serving. Maybe acceptable, but simpler: rely on Quarkus static defaults. Not required for the user's ask.

Actually the ask is automatic serving, not caching. Keep scope tight. But we should ensure `Service-Worker-Allowed` etc. already handled.

Now, Quarkus native image: `META-INF/resources` from extension jars — Quarkus automatically includes static resources in native image? I believe the static resource handling in native builds embeds resources discovered at build time from `META-INF/resources` across the classpath. Yes, Quarkus includes them (that's how Swagger UI works in native). So fine.

Now, Spring Boot: the starter jar contains `static/_pathland/...`. Its controller is a `@Controller` with `@GetMapping`, not relying on Spring's static resource handling, so the jar resources are read via `ClassPathResource`. Works in a fat jar. Good.

Now, tests to add:
- Spring starter: a test GETting the actual bundle URL `/_pathland/<bundleName>` (resolve via manifest) and asserting 200 + correct content-type + cache-control. But the test classpath's `static/_pathland` from main resources will be the committed bundle. Need a test app. Existing `BaseCssHeadersTest` uses `@SpringBootTest` with a test app. Add `DomRendererBundleTest`.
- Quarkus extension: a test GETting `/_pathland/<bundleName>` (global) and `/{app}/_pathland/<bundleName>` (mounted) asserting 200 and JS content type. But in Quarkus test, the global path is served by static resources. If the extension jar's `META-INF/resources` is on the test classpath, it should work. Add `DomRendererBundleTest` using `@QuarkusTest` + RestAssured.
- Also update existing demo tests? Maybe add nothing.

- Server-core `PathlandAssets` already resolves manifest; no change except maybe docs. But note: the demo bundle name is hash `77eb5c6fc78d`; after rebuilding and copying, hash may stay same if source unchanged. New bundle copy could be same hash. Fine.

Now, `AGENTS.md` says to update status.md for affected projects. This change affects: lib/typescript/status.md (bundle shipping), pathland-spring-boot-starter/status.md, pathland-quarkus/status.md, pathland-demo-views? no. Also README.md / AGENTS.md docs mentioning "copied into both demos". Need to update docs:
- AGENTS.md lines ~121, ~213 (DOM bundle content hash description) maybe mention shipped by starters.
- lib/typescript/README.md and status.md.
- SECURITY.md maybe.
- spec/DSL.md mentions pointer next to copies; still valid.
- docs/HARDENING.md mentions manifest; fine.

Also parent pom `refresh-ide` comment mentions bundle copied into target/classes; still valid, but now into library modules. Might adjust.

Also the `maven-resources-plugin` overwrite rationale comment mentions bundle; still fine.

Now, there's a question: should the bundle be committed to both starters or generated at build via Maven from a shared committed artifact? The repo's philosophy commits generated artifacts and CI checks drift. So commit.

Let me double check the Quarkus extension runtime jar's static resource serving and whether `META-INF/resources` in the *runtime* extension jar is served. In Quarkus, `quarkus-vertx-http` static resources default location is `META-INF/resources`; it scans the application classpath including dependencies. Yes.

But there's a known nuance: Quarkus extensions should put static resources in a **deployment** module or use `META-INF/resources` in the runtime module? Swagger UI puts them in `META-INF/resources` in runtime module. So fine.

One more nuance: If both Spring starter and Quarkus extension ship the bundle, and an app uses both (unlikely), no conflict.

Now the `copy-to-demos.mjs` also copies `sw.js` to the extension. We'll keep that or have targets include it. If we keep the extension target, sw.js already copied. Add Spring starter target. Remove demo targets.

What about `dom-renderer.current` manifest being in `META-INF/resources/_pathland/` for Quarkus and `static/_pathland/` for Spring. Both needed. The script writes both.

Now, do we want to remove demo resources entirely including the `.DS_Store`? Not relevant.

Potential concern: The Spring Boot demo's `application.properties` `spring.web.resources.cache.period=7d` may now apply to static resources; not relevant since controller handles.

Another concern: Existing library consumers who previously added their own bundle under `static/_pathland` will now have a duplicate. The app's copy wins (TCCL). Good. Should we document precedence: app-provided bundle overrides library default.

Now, should we use a new shared module instead? Let me weigh. I think the cleanest long-term is a small `pathland-web-client` (or `pathland-dom-renderer`) resource-only jar, but the user's request is specifically Spring Boot and Quarkus. The existing architecture already publishes `pathland-server-core`, `pathland-render-html`, etc. A shared jar avoids ~150KB duplication and drift. But duplication in git is already accepted for CSS? CSS lives once in `pathland-render-html/assets` and Java copies from Rust assets at build. Interesting: the CSS is not duplicated in the Java repo; Maven copies from the Rust crate assets. Could we similarly have both starters' poms copy the bundle from a single committed location (e.g., `lib/typescript/dist` is gitignored, so no). Could commit the bundle once under e.g. `lib/typescript/bundle/` or `lib/java/pathland-server-core/src/main/resources/...` and have Maven resources copy into the other module. But Maven cross-module resource copying is brittle. A resource-only module is the Maven-idiomatic way.

Let me consider creating `lib/java/pathland-web-client` (resource jar) that both `pathland-spring-boot-starter` and `pathland-quarkus` depend on. Contents:
- `META-INF/resources/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js`

parts.text:
It uses `QuarkusClassLoader.getElements("META-INF/resources", false)` and iterates over all classpath elements that are runtime, including dependency jars. So yes, dependency extension jar resources are included. And native image registers them. Great.

So Option A works for Quarkus.

Now, note the static resources processor skips if `io.quarkus.servlet` capability is present (servlet mode). Pathland uses Quarkus REST (no servlet), so fine. If an app uses a servlet extension, static resources handled by servlet. Not our concern.

Now, let me also confirm: for the mounted path, `IndexResource.deep` catches `/{app}/_pathland/...` and `frameworkFile` reads `/META-INF/resources/_pathland/<file>` via `getClass()`. In a Quarkus app, `IndexResource.class.getClassLoader()` is the runtime classloader which has all runtime elements; `getResourceAsStream` should find the extension jar's copy. Good.

Now, I'm ready to present the plan. But the system says to ask clarifying questions when weighing tradeoffs. Let me ask the artifact-strategy question. I'll present the recommended plan in text and use the question tool for the key decisions so the user can select.

Actually, the instruction says "Ask the user clarifying questions or ask for their opinion when weighing tradeoffs." I can include questions in the text, but the `question` tool is nicer. Let me use it with 2-3 questions.

Let me formulate the plan first in the message, then call question? The `question` tool call will pause and show options. I can output text before the tool call. Let me put the plan in a concise form, then ask.

Actually, in this environment, the final response should include the plan. But the `question` tool is a tool call; I can make it the last action. Better: present the plan and the open decisions as text, then invoke `question` to get the choice. But the tool output will come back to me; then I'd finalize. Since plan mode, I should end with a plan for approval, not start implementing. Let me ask the questions and then, after answers, refine the plan.

Let me call the question tool with the key decision. I'll include:
1. Bundle placement: A) duplicate into both library jars (recommended), B) single copy in server-core, C) new resource-only module.
2. Remove demo copies? Yes (recommended) / keep.
3. Rename copy script? Yes / keep name.

Let me do it. But maybe 3 questions is a lot. I'll do 2: placement and demo cleanup; the rename I'll just include in the plan as a minor step (can mention).

Actually, let me reconsider whether the recommended option should be B (server-core single copy). The downside of B is the override ambiguity, but that's manageable by adjusting lookup order.     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
    (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
    `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
    `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
    `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
    files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
    the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
    The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
    `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
    response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
    buffer issues a `Range`

    at byte 0.

  (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`

  `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).

  `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
  `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
  `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
- **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
  **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
  dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).

- `classpathFrameworkResource` (`PathlandIndexController.java:281-285`) resolves `static/_pathland/<file>` from the whole classpath, so the starter jar's copy is served at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`. App-local `static/_pathland` still wins by classpath order.

**Quarkus extension**:
- Global `/_pathland/<bundle>`: already served by Quarkus's static handler, which scans `META-INF/resources` across **all runtime classpath elements** (verified in `StaticResourcesProcessor`), so the extension jar's copy is picked up (and included in native image).

 # Pathland Project - AI Agent Guide
 
 This document provides essential context for AI agents (or human contributors) working on the **Pathland** protocol. It captures the project's direction, architectural decisions, and implementation details to ensure consistency.
 
 **Last Updated**: November 3, 2026
 
 ---
 
 ## Architecture: Rust Opcode Engine
 
 > The canonical core is a **Rust engine** that emits the application's
 > **declarative view structure** — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding,
 > alignment — as a fixed **16-byte opcode ring buffer** into shared linear
 > memory, consumed by host renderers. View components and modifiers are written
 > in Rust with a SwiftUI-like API, and in Kotlin with the hand-written
 > **`dev.pathland.view.dsl` DSL** (reusable JVM library, Java 17+); both drive the
 > engine through the flat **native C ABI** (`pathland-view-native`) over a
 > zero-copy shared ring on desktop. Java hosts mount Kotlin views through
 > `PathlandApp`.
 
 ### The 16-byte Opcode Engine
 
 - Every opcode is exactly **16 bytes**: `Category (1B) | Command ID (1B) | Flags (2B) | A (4B) | B (4B) | C (4B)`, `#[repr(C, packed)]`, little-endian.
 - A 64-byte cache line holds exactly **4 opcodes** → L1-cache-friendly.
 - Opcodes live in a **ring buffer** in linear memory; the guest writes at `writeCursor`, the host reads from `readCursor`; frame boundaries via a monotonic `frameCount` in the header block.
 - **Both directions are binary**: a second **event ring** (host → guest) carries `EVENT`-category opcodes. The renderer writes raw inputs at `eventWriteCursor`; the guest drains them at `eventReadCursor`. Events are 16-byte opcodes through the engine, never a side-channel callback.
 - **Variable-length data** (strings, token paths) lives in a bump **arena**; opcodes reference entries by offset (`[u32 byteLength][bytes...]`), so every opcode stays 16 bytes. A second host-owned **event arena** mirrors this in the host → guest direction (shared-memory event strings, e.g. `TEXT_CHANGED`); over the network, host → guest strings ride the batch's string section.
 - **Window metadata** (`META::SET_WINDOW_METADATA`, field family `TITLE`/`DESCRIPTION`/`LOCALE`) carries the hosting surface's presentation metadata; renderers map it to their own chrome (browser `<title>`/meta description/`<html lang>`, GTK/Qt window title). It is root-scoped and signal-backed, so a route title is a computed over the router. Web-only artifacts (canonical/robots/sitemap) stay host-owned.
 - Spec: **`spec/OPCODE.md`** (primary) + **`spec/CONFORMANCE.md`** (golden vectors). Companion catalogs: **`spec/PRIMITIVES.md`** (views), **`spec/MODIFIERS.md`** (modifiers/properties), **`spec/EVENTS.md`** (events), **`spec/LAYOUT.md`** (frame & layout allocation contract) — draft IDs are allocated there spec-first.
 
 ### Declarative, not positioned (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 > **The engine describes WHAT the UI is — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing,
 > padding, alignment — never WHERE it is. It does not compute layout and does
 > not emit rects.**
 
 - The engine emits **declarative structure** (`TREE` create/delete/insert/remove/move) + **constraint properties** (`PARAMETER` spacing/padding/alignment/FILL/HUG hints).
 - **Native elements everywhere**: each platform's renderer maps the opcode stream onto that platform's native elements — GTK4 widgets on desktop, DOM elements in the browser, HTML server-side — and those native elements lay themselves out. Never a generic canvas unless a platform has no native equivalent.
 - **Reactive emission**: emission is diff-based. Only the nodes that changed emit opcodes (property diffs via `SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_TEXT`, structural diffs via `TREE` opcodes). An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes. Signals in the application mark the tree dirty; the engine reconciles.
 - **Zero dynamic heap allocations** during steady-state emission (proven by test).
 
 ### no_std / wasm32 direction guard (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
 
 `pathland-core` and `pathland-view` must remain `#![no_std]` + `alloc` and
 compile for `wasm32-unknown-unknown`. This is the guarantee that the protocol
 core can still target a browser / embedded / remote projection later (goal #15,
 Quarkus SSR + WebSocket). The desktop path (`pathland-view-native`) is the only
 consumer today, but the core must not become desktop-only. Verify with
 `lib/rust/check-wasm.sh` (i.e. `cargo build -p pathland-core -p pathland-view
 --target wasm32-unknown-unknown`).
 
 ### Reactive signals (Angular-style)
 
 `pathland-core::signal` provides writable signals that live in the engine. A
 node binds its text (`Node::text_binding`), a property
 (`Node::property_bindings`) or a **string property** (`Node::string_bindings`,
 e.g. a media controller's `MEDIA_SOURCE`) to a `SignalId`; during emit the engine
 resolves the binding and records the dependency, and `Engine::set_signal`
 re-emits **only the bound nodes** (`SET_TEXT` / `SET_PROPERTY`) — no full tree
 walk. Signal values
 are one of `F32`/`U32`/`Bool`/`Enum`/`Str` (packed to the wire's `u32` value or
 arena string). Foreign hosts reach signals via the flat C ABI
 (`pathland_native_signal_create_*` / `signal_set_*` / `node_bind_text` /
 `node_bind_property`) and the Kotlin/JVM `Signal` type. Binding then calling `emit`
 records the dependency; a subsequent `set` is a partial emit. (Computed/derived
 signals + effects are the planned next step.)
